messages:
Ashley: Heads-up — opened PR #4921 updating VPC peering, GPU pool attachment, and a small route-table refactor for prod-eu. Need 2 infra approvals before the merge window at 09:00 UTC tomorrow. Can someone take a look? https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4921 :hourglass:
Samir: Will check. Which regions will be affected? Any rolling plan?
Ashley: Only prod-eu for the changes in this PR. Plan is canary on two nodes, then full attach. I added a canary tag to the module and a fallback that detaches if healthcheck fails.

Liam: Noted. Main risk is route propagation timing — if the new route table gets a higher priority we could blackhole cross-az traffic for a minute. I’ll look at the route change and the order in the TF plan.
Eva: :eyes: I can run the TF plan locally and validate the route priorities. Also can you paste the minimal tf snippet for the attach logic?

Ashley: Sure — snippet below (only the changed bits):
```hcl
module \"gpu_pool_attachment\" {
  source = \"./modules/gpu_attachment\"
  pool_id = var.gpu_pool_id
  vpc_id  = var.vpc_id
  canary  = var.canary_enabled
}
resource \"aws_route_table_association\" \"gpu_assoc\" {
  subnet_id = aws_subnet.gpu_subnet.id
  route_table_id = aws_route_table.gpu_rt.id
}
```
Also updated a toggle var `canary_enabled` (default false).
Marta: Quick nit: module input is `pool_id` but we use `gpu_pool_id` elsewhere — can we standardize to avoid confusion? Small rename in the module vars would help audits. I left a comment in the PR.
infra-bot: CI / tfsec: all checks passed ✅ — plan looks clean. (plan artifact: https://ci.redwood/infra/4921/plan)

Samir: Re: validation, run:
````bash
export TF_VAR_canary_enabled=true
terraform init && terraform plan -var=\"gpu_pool_id=pool-eu-1\" -out=plan.out
terraform show -json plan.out | jq '.resource_changes[] | select(.address|test(\"route_table_association\"))'
````
That will surface risky association changes.
Liam: I ran the plan locally, left an approval and one comment about the route priority. After Marta's variable tweak and Ashley’s canary smoke, I can approve the second one tonight.
Eva: Verified the plan looks like it will create one association for canary subnets then the rest. No overlapping higher-priority routes found. Leaving an approve now.

Marta: Approved after renaming pool_id -> gpu_pool_id in the module. Left a doc note.
Ashley: thanks all. I requested a canary hold in the console so we can manually unhold once smoke checks pass. Will merge after the second approval and do a 15m watch.
Ashley: Final: merging at 08:30 UTC tomorrow to give some runway before the 09:00 window. Will post a deployment checklist in #eng-oncall and ping SRE. :rocket:
